name: DJ Slip
sources: style-research-extended vol.1 g-funk — DJ Slip (Compton's Most Wanted)
notes: The research calls this the sparsest programming in the whole section, and every drum number here is chosen to be the lowest in the batch: kick at 1–3 a bar with the secondary anchor moved off the and-of-2 to a plain 3, `syncopation` 0.12, `tresilloBias` 0.05, ghost notes at 0.04, one percussion lane, and a snare velocity tier lowered because the research says the snare is thin and dry. Against that, the harmony is the *lushest* thing here — Isaac Hayes and Teddy Pendergrass sources give 7th and 9th colour, so `extensions.ninth` is 0.3 while `melody.densityPerBar` is 1–3. That contrast is the entry. `chords.impliedByRiff` is set because the harmony is one sustained Rhodes or string loop, and the chord part's variety comes from `chordDurationBeats` and three harmonic rhythms over a very wide voicing register rather than from chord changes. The uncredited freestyle keyboardist Willie Zimmerman is why `quantizeStrength` drops to 0.7 — improvised, non-quantized keyboard lines. ⛔ The bass is `mirror_kick` at 0.95, not `reese_sustain`: the research says long sustained sub, slow-moving, few notes, and over a kick that plays 1 and 3 that reads as sustained without collapsing the part to one note per chord. ⚠ The research says the kick often halves so the record reads half-time; `session.halfTime` stays false and the halving is expressed in `kick.densityPerBar` instead, because flipping the session flag would halve the hats and the backbeat too. ⚠ `medium` per the research's medium-high. ⚠ **The bass pool was widened after `bass.rs` measured it at 0.830 distinct against a floor of 0.95.** It was authored with NO passing tones, followRootsProb 0.95, anticipationProb 0.03 over register [22,40] — a faithful description of a sample-loop bass, and one that leaves a seed nothing to vary but root and octave. Now ["P5"], root lock 0.88, anticipation 0.2, register [22,44]. The line is still overwhelmingly root-on-kick; what changed is how many different records it can be, not how busy any one of them is. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 44 to 43 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 44 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 1. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 880 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3, densityRatio 0.5, melody density [1,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary.
